rows.requirement: INPUT ACCESS: a processor candidate is only emitted where the corp can actually source every input of its chosen recipe on that body — pool + local market inventory, measured against the same coverage threshold the production tick uses. Read const: scoring never authors a pool.

rows.requirement: THE PHASE VOCABULARY IS DERIVED ONCE. The card's phase readout and the dispatch line's phrasing come from the SAME read_battle_phase call in the world layer, so the two surfaces cannot describe the same fight differently. Assert structurally - one derivation site - rather than by comparing two strings.
rows.result_metric: 6/6 phase values reachable

rows.requirement: THE DISPATCH LAYER CONSUMES NO DRAW. Phrase selection folds stream_seed with the round index rather than drawing, so text generation is structurally unable to move the simulation. Assert that the same fight replays to the same lines AND that wording varies across rounds of one fight - a bank that never varies and a bank that varies non-deterministically fail the same check from opposite sides.
rows.result_metric: 10 dispatches -> 6 distinct lines
rows.notes: B14e asserts replay-identity; B14f asserts variation. B14f's measured result is the interesting one: 10 dispatches from one fight produced 6 distinct lines, so the fold is live rather than degenerate.

rows.requirement: THE QUOTED PRICE IS THE CHARGED PRICE. What the card says withdrawing costs equals what withdrawing actually charges, in all three terms. The hazard is a second copy of the resolver's arithmetic inside the card drifting from the resolver's own.
rows.result_metric: quote == charge, 3/3 terms
rows.notes: B12b asserts quote_withdrawal() against the charge the resolver applies. Structurally the card cannot drift: it renders the quote rather than recomputing anything.

(4) The base rate is 17 of 32 (53%) in this fixture, not 2 of 8 - zero-war is the MODAL outcome, which makes the underlying defect more urgent and not less. world-save-snapshot.resolution: LANDED 2026-08-22. The world snapshot (IOSV) plus the save-game envelope (IOSG) - one .iosave file, field-wise flat binary, atomic on failure at both levels. Reachable four ways: F5/F6 quick slots, --load <path>, and verify.save/verify.load for capture scripts. Two findings worth carrying out of the work: corp_modifiers is not recomputable and had to be serialised (NR-510), and verify.command had never routed through dispatch_action, so every app-level command it named silently did nothing.
